facts.statement: The genus Camuropiscis was described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Fossils of Camuropiscis date to the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Camuropiscis lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are four recorded fossil occurrences of Camuropiscis.
Camuropiscis fossils have been found in the Gogo Formation in Kimberley, Western Australia.
facts.quote: found at the Gogo Formation of Kimberley, Western Australia

facts.statement: Camuropiscis species possessed a flattened, elongated snout that likely improved their hydrodynamic streamlining.
facts.quote: The species of Camuropiscis had a flattened, elongated snout that may have aided in enhancing its hydrodynamic streamlining.

facts.statement: The name Camuropiscis translates to "flat-nosed fish."
Camuropiscis is classified within the class Placodermi.
Camuropiscis belongs to the family Camuropiscidae.
Camuropiscis is part of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the larger group Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Camuropiscis is a member of the family Camuropiscidae under the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Camuropiscis is Camuropiscis concinnus.

rejected.statement: Camuropiscis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm.
rejected.quote: Camuropiscis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm
